description: Somos un equipo de cinco estudiantes de grado once que compartimos el deseo de aprender, crear y asumir nuevos retos. Nos caracterizamos por ser unidos, responsables, creativos y comprometidos. Valoramos las ideas de todos y creemos que nuestras diferencias nos ayudan a encontrar mejores soluciones. Más que participar, queremos aportar una idea, aprender de cada experiencia y demostrar que, con confianza, esfuerzo y trabajo en equipo, podemos transformar buenas ideas en grandes proyectos juntos.
summary:
Lunar Command is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) educational mission trainer built for learners aged 7 to 12+ to experience the real-world physics and teamwork required to survive at the Moon's South Pole. Inspired by NASA's Artemis program and set in Shackleton Crater, the web application challenges young commanders to manage electricity, air and water recycling, hydroponic food, radiation shielding, and crew morale through branching, card-based decisions and interactive colony mini-games.

To address the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, Lunar Command adapts its interface by age group—simplifying complex telemetry into three visual pillars for ages 7–9 while offering full five-system management for older students—and includes built-in voice narration via the Web Speech API. The simulation connects live space weather alerts from the NASA DONKI Solar Flare API (with a curated offline archive fallback) and translates real NASA OSDR biological studies into kid-friendly science facts, helping students develop critical thinking, resource literacy, and STEM curiosity without requiring downloads or logins.
details:
A. What It Does

Lunar Command is a web-based educational survival and mission-training game set at Shackleton Crater on the Moon's South Pole. Players step into the role of a Junior Lunar Commander leading a 36-member crew through a multi-act expedition (65 to 90 lunar days/Sols). Rather than passively reading about space exploration, players actively manage the base's daily survival by responding to mission cards, crew dilemmas, space weather alerts, and facility maintenance tasks.

B. How It Works

At the heart of Lunar Command is a deterministic colony physics and decision engine. Each turn represents one lunar day and presents a situation with contrasting choices (Option A, Option B, and occasionally a third Option C). Every decision applies transparent, balanced effects across five core systems: Electric Power, Air & Water (ECLSS), Food & Greenhouse, Radiation Shielding, and Crew Morale.

Dynamic events—such as solar particle storms, lunar dust accumulation, equipment wear, and crew trust shifts—keep each expedition engaging. Players can inspect an interactive SVG colony map, trigger emergency protocols like the Underground Radiation Shelter, play 8 organic terrain mini-games, and review their progress across 3 campaign Acts with checkpoints at Sol 20 and Sol 45. Upon completing the mission, players receive a personalized, downloadable PNG Junior Astronaut Commander Diploma summarizing their science score and survival decisions.

C. Educational Value

Lunar Command promotes experiential STEM learning, critical thinking, and cause-and-effect reasoning. Instead of memorizing isolated facts, students see how conserving battery power affects greenhouse lighting or how shielding protects crew health during a solar flare. After key decisions, the game pairs the narrative outcome with a concise, age-appropriate NASA Science Fact explaining the real-world physics or biology behind the event. Built-in contextual helpers clarify technical terms like "humidity condenser" or "regolith" in plain language.

D. Intended Impact

Our goal is to make space exploration concepts approachable for elementary and middle-school students (ages 7–12+), families, and classrooms, regardless of whether they speak English or Spanish or have a fast internet connection. Because the app runs in any modern browser without logins and includes an offline-ready NASA data fallback, it is designed to be easily adopted in both home and school settings. (Note: Formal classroom pilot studies have not yet been conducted; educational impact is currently an intended goal supported by the game's pedagogical design.)

E. Technology and Development

Lunar Command is built as a client-side single-page application using React 19, TypeScript, and Vite 6, styled with Tailwind CSS 4, Lucide React icons, and Motion for smooth UI transitions. The game's simulation logic, seeded random generator, and 13 distinct ending states are separated into a pure TypeScript engine verified by 105 automated tests across 22 suites (including Monte Carlo strategy balancing) using tsx.

For live space weather, the app queries the NASA DONKI Solar Flare API (api.nasa.gov/DONKI/FLR) using a 6-hour localStorage cache and a curated historical archive fallback. Voice narration is powered natively by the browser's Web Speech API, and the application is deployed on Vercel.

F. Creativity and Innovation

Inspired by swipe-based decision games, Lunar Command combines narrative storytelling with a genuine physical resource model—ensuring no resource increases without physical production (e.g., solar arrays, greenhouses, or repair workshops). Its age-adaptive HUD dynamically transforms the same underlying simulation from 3 simplified visual pillars (for ages 7–9) into 5 detailed engineering systems (for ages 10–12+), allowing siblings, parents, and students of different ages to enjoy the same mission at their own level.

G. Design Considerations

Accessibility and clarity guided every design choice. We implemented instant bilingual switching (English/Spanish), a "Listen" button on cards and science facts for early readers, high-contrast warm-paper aesthetics for comfortable reading, and a dedicated "Quick Moments (60s Demo)" mode so educators and judges can immediately test key scenarios without playing through dozens of turns.
